_comment: Customer-facing subscription strings the public App Store Connect API will not let us change, recorded so the next pass does not rediscover them.
finding: All 64 subscription localizations (4 products x 16 locales) and all 16 subscription-group localizations are refused by the API. Two things are wrong in them: pro_annual_standard's display names still read 'Glovebox Pro (...)' and every group localization still reads 'Glovebox Pro', and every product description still reads 'Unlimited vehicles and custom service intervals' - which was the freemium delta and is now simply the whole app.
targetValues: store/pro_annual.json, store/pro_annual_standard.json, store/pro_monthly.json, store/pro_weekly.json (name + description per locale) and store/subscription-group-localizations.json (group name). All within Apple's 30-char name and 45-char description limits.
blocker: PATCH /v1/subscriptionLocalizations/{id} and /v1/subscriptionGroupLocalizations/{id} both return: 'Cannot edit SubscriptionLocalization when it is in ACTIVE state'. The subscriptions are APPROVED and live, so their customer-facing strings are locked the way a READY_FOR_SALE version locks name and description. `asc subscriptions localizations sync` fails all 16 per product with the same error, and `asc web` has no localization surface either - availability and pricing only.
remedy: Edit the display names and descriptions in the App Store Connect web UI, per locale, from the values in the store/pro_*.json files. The edit moves each subscription to 'Ready to Submit' and it is reviewed alongside an app version.

Once one subscription has a pending version in App Store Connect, retry `asc subscriptions localizations sync --subscription-id <id> --input store/<product>.json` - the API refusal is about the ACTIVE state, so a subscription with an editable pending version may accept the rest without hand-typing 16 locales.
doneViaApi: Internal reference names are now Wrenchy Pro (Annual/Annual, no trial/Monthly/Weekly), and pro_annual_standard's review note no longer describes a free tier or a 3-day trial on the wrong product. None of those are customer-facing.
notBlockingRelease: These strings appear on the StoreKit sheet, not in the App Store listing. 1.0.1 and 1.2.0 both passed `asc validate` with them outstanding.
